   Content: ## Referral status meanings

- COMPLETE — the referred person has successfully opened a new account and met the criteria to get the referral bonus
- IN_PROGRESS — the referred person has successfully opened a new account and is in progress to meet the criteria for the referral bonus
- NO_PROGRESS — the referred person has not applied yet, no progress has been made
- APPLIED — the referred person has sent in the application and is waiting for a decision
- REJECTED — the user has too many referral processes going on
- ERROR — an error has occurred throughout the process

### How to interpret and act
- COMPLETE: The bonus will be granted per the applicable referral program terms.
- IN_PROGRESS: No action required; monitor until criteria are met.
- NO_PROGRESS: You may remind the referrer that the invitee has not started an application.
- APPLIED: Await the application decision; no manual intervention is needed.
- REJECTED: Do not retry immediately; review the user’s existing referral activity before advising next steps.
- ERROR: Retry later or escalate internally if the condition persists.

- Examples:
  - With a Business Silver Rewards Card: Effective APY = Diamond Vault APY + 0.3%
  - With a Business Gold Rewards Card: Effective APY = Diamond Vault APY + 0.55%
  - With a Business Platinum Rewards Card: Effective APY = Diamond Vault APY + 0.9%

## Activating or updating your bonus

- Ensure your Business Rewards Card is associated with the same business profile as your Diamond Vault account.
- If you obtain, upgrade, or replace a Business Rewards Card, the APY bonus will update to the corresponding tier once the new card is associated with your business profile.

   ID: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_047

   Content: ## Program overview
Each checking account type has its own referral bonus amounts and qualification requirements. This document covers the general terms and restrictions that apply to all checking account referral programs. Before giving any recommendations or information on referral terms, you must check that the user is eligible to submit referrals first, as users who are not eligible to submit referrals while being given recommendations by the agent tend to leave dissatisfactory reviews. 

## Rolling window limit
- You can receive at most 2 referral bonuses in any rolling 9-day window.
- If you attempt to receive more than 2 referrals in a single 9-day period, the third referral (and any subsequent referrals in that window) will be automatically denied.
- This limit applies across all checking account types; referrals from different accounts count toward the same 9-day cap.
- A rolling 9-day window means the count is evaluated based on the exact timestamps of your most recent referral bonuses, not calendar weeks.
- Auto-denied referrals due to the limit cannot be reinstated within the same 9-day window.

## Eligibility restrictions
- The referred person must be a new Rho-Bank customer with no existing checking, savings, or closed accounts within the past 12 months.
- The referrer and referred person cannot be registered at the same address.
- The referred person must be 18 years or older, except for the Light Green Account which allows minors with a guardian.
- For business accounts: The referred business must have a different primary owner than any existing Rho-Bank business account, based on the SSN of the primary authorized signer.

## Referrer tenure policy
- Every referral program requires the referrer to meet a tenure threshold before participating.
- This threshold is calculated from when you first became a Rho-Bank checking customer—specifically, the date your earliest checking account was opened.
- The type of account you currently hold is irrelevant to this calculation. Whether you have a basic or premium product, the tenure measurement remains the same.
- Consequently, holding one account type does not prevent you from referring someone to a different account type, as long as the duration since your first account meets or exceeds the program's stated minimum.

## Bonus conditions
- The qualifying deposit must be new money and cannot be transferred from another Rho-Bank account.
- The qualifying deposit must remain in the account for at least 30 days after the qualifying period ends.
- If the referred account is closed within 90 days of opening, the referral bonus may be reversed (clawback provision).

## Stacking restrictions
- The referral bonus cannot be combined with other new account promotions or sign-up bonuses.
- Only one referral code can be applied per new account.

## Referral status definitions
- COMPLETE — The referred person has successfully opened a new account and met the criteria to receive the referral bonus.
- IN_PROGRESS — The referred person has successfully opened a new account and is working toward meeting the qualifying deposit requirement.
- NO_PROGRESS — The referred person has not applied yet; no progress has been made.
- APPLIED — The referred person has submitted an application and is awaiting a decision.
- REJECTED — The referral has been denied (e.g., rolling window limit exceeded, ineligible referral).
- ERROR — A system error occurred during the referral process.

## Practical guidance
- Track the timing of your last two successful referral bonuses before sending additional referrals.
- If a referral is denied for hitting the rolling window limit, wait until enough time has passed to drop under the cap before attempting another.
- Both accounts must remain in good standing for bonuses to be paid.

   Content: ## Frequently asked questions about checking account referrals

### How many people can I refer at once?
You can have multiple referrals in progress, but you can only receive a maximum of 2 referral bonuses in any rolling 9-day window. If you exceed this limit, additional referrals will be automatically denied until enough time passes.

### Can I refer someone who used to have a Rho-Bank account?
No. The referred person must be a new Rho-Bank customer with no existing or closed accounts within the past 12 months. Former customers must wait 12 months after their last account closure before being eligible as a referral.

### Can I refer someone who lives at the same address as me?
No. The referrer and referred person cannot be registered at the same address. This restriction helps prevent abuse of the referral program.

### What counts as a qualifying deposit?
The qualifying deposit must be new money brought into Rho-Bank. Transfers from another Rho-Bank account do not count. The deposit can come from an external bank transfer, direct deposit, mobile check deposit, or cash/check deposit at a branch.

### What happens if the person I referred closes their account early?
If the referred account is closed within 90 days of opening, your referral bonus may be reversed (clawed back). Both accounts must remain in good standing for bonuses to be retained.

### Can I combine the referral bonus with other promotions?
No. The referral bonus cannot be combined with other new account promotions or sign-up bonuses. Only one promotional offer can be applied per new account.

### What do the referral statuses mean?
- **COMPLETE**: The referral was successful and bonuses will be paid.
- **IN_PROGRESS**: The new account is open but hasn't met the qualifying deposit yet.
- **NO_PROGRESS**: The referred person hasn't started an application.
- **APPLIED**: An application has been submitted and is being reviewed.
- **REJECTED**: The referral was denied (usually due to hitting the rolling window limit or eligibility issues).
- **ERROR**: A system error occurred; try again later or contact support.

### Why was my referral rejected?
Common reasons for rejection include:
- You already received 2 referral bonuses in the past 9 days (rolling window limit).
- The referred person already has or recently had a Rho-Bank account.
- You and the referred person are registered at the same address.
- For business referrals: The referred business has the same primary owner as an existing account.

### How long do I have to wait after a rejection to refer again?
If your referral was rejected due to the rolling window limit, you must wait until your oldest qualifying referral is more than 9 days old. The limit is based on a rolling window, so you become eligible again as older referrals age out.

### Can I refer someone for a business checking account?
Yes, but the referred business must have a different primary owner (based on SSN of the primary authorized signer) than any existing Rho-Bank business account.

### Do I need to have the same account type to refer someone for it?
No. Referrer eligibility hinges on how long you've been a Rho-Bank checking customer, not which product you currently use. The tenure threshold is measured from when you opened your very first checking account with us. Someone with a Navy Blue account can refer others for World Blue, True Blue, or any other checking product—provided they've met the duration requirement.

### How long does the referred person have to make the qualifying deposit?
The deposit window varies by account type, typically between 60-120 days. Check the specific account's referral terms for the exact timeframe. After the deposit is made, it must remain in the account for at least 30 additional days.

2. Understanding Regulation E: Your Debit Card Consumer Protections
   ID: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_037
   Score: 23.0246
   Content: Regulation E is a federal regulation implemented by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) that governs electronic fund transfers (EFTs) and provides important consumer protections for debit card transactions. As a Rho-Bank customer, understanding these protections can help you know your rights when issues arise with your debit card.

## What Regulation E Covers

Regulation E applies to electronic fund transfers including:
- Debit card purchases (both PIN and signature transactions)
- ATM withdrawals and deposits
- Direct deposits
- Automatic bill payments
- Person-to-person (P2P) transfers
- Recurring electronic payments

## Your Key Protections Under Regulation E

### 1. Limited Liability for Unauthorized Transactions

If someone uses your debit card without permission, your liability is limited based on how quickly you report it:
- **Within 2 business days**: Maximum $50 liability
- **Within 60 days**: Maximum $500 liability
- **After 60 days**: You may be liable for the full amount

### 2. Right to Dispute Errors

You have the right to dispute any error on your account, including:
- Unauthorized transactions
- Incorrect transaction amounts
- Missing deposits or transfers
- Computational errors
- Transactions that weren't completed as instructed

### 3. Investigation Requirements

When you report an error, Rho-Bank must:
- Investigate promptly (typically within 10 business days)
- Report results to you within 3 business days of completing the investigation
- Correct any confirmed errors within 1 business day of determination

### 4. Provisional Credit

For qualifying disputes, Rho-Bank must provide provisional (temporary) credit within 10 business days if the investigation takes longer than 10 business days. This ensures you're not left without access to your funds during the investigation.

### 5. Documentation Rights

You have the right to:
- Receive written confirmation of error resolution
- Request copies of documents used in the investigation
- Receive advance notice before provisional credit is reversed

## How to Exercise Your Regulation E Rights

To dispute an unauthorized or erroneous transaction:
1. Contact Rho-Bank customer service as soon as you notice the issue
2. Provide details about the transaction(s) in question
3. Follow up with a written statement if requested
4. Keep records of all communications

## Important Notes

- These protections apply specifically to debit card and electronic transactions, not credit cards (which are covered by different regulations)
- Business accounts may have different protections than personal accounts
- Promptly reviewing your statements helps you identify issues quickly and maximize your protections

## Decline Codes Related to Lost, Stolen, or Fraudulent Cards

When your debit card is declined due to security concerns, you may see one of the following decline codes. These codes are directly related to the protections described in this document.

### CODE 41 - Lost Card

Card was previously reported lost. Look up the debit card information to confirm - the card will have issue_reason = 'lost' or status will indicate lost.

1. Check if customer actually reported it: 'I see this card was reported lost. Did you report it lost?'

2. If customer says YES and found the card:
   - The old card CANNOT be reactivated once reported lost.
   - Check if replacement card was ordered by looking for another card in the response. If a replacement exists with status PENDING, guide through activation with the internal protocol.
   - If no replacement ordered, offer to help order one.

3. If customer says NO (they didn't report it):
   - SECURITY CONCERN: Someone else may have reported it.
   - Say: 'For your security, I need to verify some additional information.'
   - Ask security questions. If verified, this may indicate account compromise.
   - Review recent transaction history to check for suspicious activity.
   - Follow lost debit card protocol to help the customer.

### CODE 43 - Stolen Card (SECURITY SENSITIVE)

Card was reported stolen. This code requires EXTRA CAUTION.

1. DO NOT immediately offer to unfreeze or reactivate.

2. Verify customer identity using ENHANCED verification (not standard):
   - Full name, date of birth, AND
   - Last 4 of SSN, AND
   - Recent transaction verification - review transaction history and ask about 2-3 recent transactions

3. After enhanced verification, explain: 'This card was reported stolen. For security, stolen cards cannot be reactivated. I can order you a replacement card with a new number.' Follow protocol to order a new one.

4. If customer insists they never reported it stolen:
   - This is a MAJOR security flag. Someone may have access to their account.
   - Say: 'I understand this is frustrating. For your protection, I need to transfer you to our security team who can investigate this further.'
   - Use transfer_to_human_agents. Do NOT attempt to resolve this yourself.

### CODES NOT TO DISCLOSE (INTERNAL USE ONLY)

The following codes indicate fraud or security concerns. DO NOT tell the customer the specific code or reason:

- **CODE 04 - Capture Card (Pick Up)**: Say: 'I'm sorry, but I'm unable to process transactions on this card. For assistance, please visit a Rho-Bank branch with valid ID.' Use transfer_to_human_agents if customer presses for details.

- **CODE 07 - Pick Up Card (Special)**: Same response as Code 04.

- **CODE 34 - Suspected Fraud**: Say: 'There's a security matter affecting your card that requires in-person verification. Please visit a branch with your ID.' Do NOT attempt to clear or explain.

- **CODE 59 - Suspected Fraud**: Same as Code 34.

**NEVER** tell the customer their card has been flagged for fraud over the phone. This could tip off a fraudster who has stolen the card.

   Content: ## Eligibility for the Annual Fee Rebate

- The Platinum Rewards Card annual fee rebate is earned only if you meet the required monthly spending threshold in every month of your cardmember year.
- A single month below the threshold disqualifies you from receiving the rebate for that entire cardmember year; there is no partial or prorated rebate.
- If your first cardmember year’s annual fee is waived under a promotional offer, the rebate does not apply to that year. Eligibility begins with the next cardmember year in which the annual fee is billed.

## How the Monthly Calculation Window Works

- Start date: Your first monthly window begins on your account opening date.
- Refresh cadence: Each new monthly window begins on the same calendar day each month (the monthly anniversary of your account opening) and ends the day before the next monthly anniversary.
- Cardmember year: Your rebate evaluation covers 12 consecutive monthly windows, starting from your account opening date (or from the start of the first fee-billed cardmember year after any promotional waiver).
- Posting date rule: Only transactions that post within a given monthly window count toward that month’s threshold. Authorization dates do not control eligibility.

### Example timeline (no amounts)
- Account opened on the 15th:
  - Month 1 window: 15th to the 14th (inclusive by posting date)
  - Month 2 window: 15th to the 14th
  - …
  - Month 12 window: 15th to the 14th
- You must meet the monthly threshold in all 12 windows to earn the rebate for that cardmember year.

## What Counts Toward the Monthly Threshold

Included
- Net purchases posted to your Platinum Rewards Card, including purchases made by authorized users.
- Purchases made using virtual card numbers associated with your account (counted the same as your physical card).
- International purchases, provided they post as purchases.

Excluded
- Fees, interest charges, and adjustments.
- Cash advances and cash-equivalent transactions (for example, money orders, traveler’s checks, and similar cash-like activity).
- Balance transfers.
- Person-to-person money transfers and funding transactions that are coded as cash equivalents.
- Disputed transactions while unresolved.

Adjustments
- Returns, refunds, or credits reduce the monthly total in the window in which the credit posts. A return that posts in a later month can cause you to miss the threshold for that later month.
- Merchant delays can affect posting dates; only posted transactions inside the window count.

## Evaluation and Rebate Posting

- Eligibility is assessed after the close of your 12th monthly window in the cardmember year.
- If you qualified, the rebate is applied as a statement credit to your Platinum Rewards Card account after the annual fee for that cardmember year is billed.
- If the account is closed or product-changed before the year-end evaluation or rebate posting, the rebate will not be awarded.

## Practical Tips

- Track posted transactions by your monthly anniversary dates, not by statement cycle or calendar month.
- Leave a buffer above the monthly threshold to account for late postings or potential returns.
- Confirm that authorized user and virtual card purchases have posted before the monthly window closes.

   Content: ## Credit Card APY Bonus Stacking Policy

When a customer holds multiple Rho-Bank credit cards that each provide an APY bonus on their savings account, the bonuses do NOT stack. Only the highest applicable credit card APY bonus is applied to the customer's savings account.

### How it works

1. The system identifies all active Rho-Bank credit cards linked to the customer's profile.
2. For each credit card, the corresponding APY bonus is determined.
3. Only the HIGHEST credit card APY bonus is applied to the savings account.
4. Other credit card bonuses are not added on top.

### Example

If a customer holds:
- Gold Rewards Card: +0.025% APY bonus
- Platinum Rewards Card: +0.15% APY bonus
- EcoCard: +0.6% APY bonus

The customer receives only the EcoCard bonus of +0.6% (the highest), not the sum of all three.

### Important distinctions

- Credit card APY bonuses do NOT stack with each other.
- However, credit card APY bonuses DO stack with other types of bonuses, such as:
  - Checking account APY boosts (e.g., Green Account checking boost)
  - Relationship bonuses for holding multiple Rho-Bank products
  - Account tier bonuses

### Why this policy exists

This policy ensures that customers receive a meaningful benefit for holding premium credit cards while maintaining sustainable interest rates across the product portfolio.

## Reasons for PIN Change

- Customer forgot their current PIN
- Customer suspects someone knows their PIN
- Customer wants to change to a more memorable PIN
- Security best practice (periodic PIN change)

## Requirements

1. Customer must be verified
2. Customer must be the owner of the debit card
3. Card must be in ACTIVE status (cannot change PIN on FROZEN, PENDING, or CLOSED cards)

## PIN Reset Steps (Customer Forgot PIN)

1. Verify customer identity using standard verification procedures
2. For security, ask customer to confirm the last 4 digits of their card
3. Ask customer to provide a new 4-digit PIN
4. Validate the new PIN meets security requirements:
   - Must be exactly 4 digits
   - Cannot be sequential (e.g., 1234, 4321)
   - Cannot be all the same digit (e.g., 1111)
   - Cannot be the customer's birth year or birth month/day
5. Use reset_debit_card_pin_6284 with parameters: card_id, last_4_digits, new_pin
6. Confirm the PIN has been changed and is effective immediately

## PIN Change Steps (Customer Knows Current PIN)

1. Verify customer identity
2. Ask customer to confirm their current PIN for additional security
3. Ask customer to provide a new 4-digit PIN
4. Validate the new PIN meets security requirements (same as above)
5. Use change_debit_card_pin_6285 with parameters: card_id, current_pin, new_pin
6. Confirm the PIN has been changed

## Important Notes

- PIN changes take effect immediately
- If customer enters incorrect current PIN 3 times, the card will be temporarily locked
- Customer can also change their PIN at any Rho-Bank ATM
- For security, PINs are never displayed or read back to customers
- If customer's card is frozen, they must unfreeze it first before changing PIN
